title: Protest outside Czech TV in Prague in support of abolishing broadcasting fees
seoTitle: Prague protest against public TV fees

tea.why: Protesters gathered to support government plans to abolish broadcasting fees and demand reforms to public media.
tea.want: Abolition of television and radio broadcasting fees and changes to the functioning of Czech Television.
tea.changed: Nov 7: Several hundred people gathered outside Czech TV in Prague, featuring speeches by politicians and critics.

summary: On Saturday afternoon, a demonstration took place outside the Czech Television building on Kavčí hory in Prague. Organized by the Svatopluk association, participants marched from the Congress Centre to the main television building to support government plans to eliminate broadcasting fees and demand reforms for Czech Television and Czech Radio. Speakers included Svatopluk chairman Petr Drulák, politicians Kateřina Konečná and Ivan David, and actor Oldřich Kaiser. A counter-demonstration of several dozen supporters of public media also gathered at the scene, with some arriving on motorcycles to disrupt speeches. According to police reports, one man was reported to authorities for allegedly disrupting the gathering. Dozens of police officers supervised the event, which lasted about two and a half hours and ended without major incidents.
demands: Abolish television and radio broadcasting fees
Implement changes to the functioning of Czech Television
response: According to police, one man was reported to authorities for allegedly disrupting the assembly with loud speech. Dozens of police officers supervised the demonstration, which proceeded without major issues.
